Q116276105.summary: In a row of shell-topped niches beneath a frieze of vines with harvesting putti, the apostles stand in pairs as Christ, at the centre, raises his right hand. This is the 'traditio legis', Christ giving the Law to St Peter as leader of the Church, with St Paul standing beside to acknowledge Peter's authority. Christ's face has been worn away, but his commanding gesture still holds the composition together.
facts: The Met explains that the Church of Rome developed this image in the late 4th century to stress the primacy of St Peter, traditionally the first bishop of Rome, and that it spread widely through western Europe.
Besides Peter and Paul, four further apostles survive on this fragment.
The scene is set within a traditional Roman sarcophagus form: niches framed by columns with putti in vine scrolls above.
Q116276105.notes: The scroll offered to Peter, mentioned by the Met, is not clearly legible in the thumbnail.
